blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-privacy-1 (The address pattern misses valid and encoded addresses, which reach the logs in full) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.recommendation: The module promises it "never writes a full e-mail address" and the proposal says every address in the message and the fields is masked, but the pattern only matches an ASCII local part made of `A-Za-z0-9._%+-` followed by a literal `@` and an ASCII domain. Each of these goes to the hosting provider's logs (kept 90 days) unmasked or partly masked: `logInfo("GET /reset?email=ada.lovelace%40example.org")` (percent-encoded `@`, as in a logged URL or query string) is written whole; `ada.lovelace@exämple.org` (internationalized domain) and `"ada lovelace"@example.org` (quoted local part) do not match and are written whole; `o'brien@example.org` matches only from `b` and is logged as `o'b***@example.org`, leaking the start of the local part. GDPR Art. 5(1)(c) data minimisation and Art. 25 data protection by design. Fix: decode or also match `%40` (case-insensitive), widen the local part to the RFC 5322 atext characters and quoted strings, accept non-ASCII domain labels, and add a test per form.
findings.title: The address pattern misses valid and encoded addresses, which reach the logs in full

findings.evidence:
for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(fields)) {
  safe[key] = typeof value === "string" ? maskEmails(value) : value;
findings.recommendation: Only field values go through `maskEmails`; the keys are copied as they come. A caller that keys fields by address, e.g. `logInfo("retries", { [user.email]: 3 })`, writes the full address to the logs. No caller exists yet, so this depends on future use. Mask the keys too (`safe[maskEmails(key)]`), or document that keys must never hold personal data.
findings.title: Field keys are written to the log without masking

findings.recommendation: `a***@example.org` keeps the initial and the whole domain. For a personal or small-organization domain (e.g. `a***@lovelace-family.org`) the masked form can still single out the person, so it remains personal data in logs kept 90 days. Whether such domains appear depends on the customer base, not visible here. If the domain is not needed for debugging, mask it too, or replace the address by a keyed hash so log lines stay correlatable.
findings.title: The mask keeps the first letter and the full domain
